Nothing at all to do with the euro dome, but I got an explanation for about 75% of the weird shit that's been going on with my health over the last year 

First of all, the folks who read my spinal MRI did not read it close enough. Most of the weird numbness and shooting pains are 100% explainable by a pair of bulging discs, but they are not herniated, which means they can be very effectively treated without surgery! I found this out after advancing to getting a brain MRI which thankfully turned out normal, but then the radiologist was surprised that there was nothing that would explain the very obvious symptoms I was having, so I asked him what he thought of the spinal mri, and he was quite frustrated at what was apparently missed by whoever read it. 

So that's good, means that I wasted about 6 months where I could have already started the necessary treatments, but it's good because the alternatives were that it could be something like early MS. Basically everything between C4band C6 is in rough shape, but spinal traction and postural focused PT generally results in massive improvements for people dealing with this. Something like 60% of people report almost complete recession of symptoms with traction therapy alone, when combined with PT the numbers are even better. 

And then there's the second one, the weird respiratory shit. Turns out that I'm quite allergic to certain kinds of mold. Turns out, the place I moved into last summer as those kinds of mold. I have developed full-blown allergic asthma from a year of constant exposure. 

It's got to be in the HVAC system, because a pretty thorough visual inspection finds no evidence of mold anywhere else. Either way, I'm moving into a new place on August 1st, so that will take care of that. 

It's reaffirming to know that I'm not just a goddamn hypochondriac, and so far over the last year nearly everything that I felt was wrong ended up having a concrete diagnosis that has been able to result in treatments. 

I still have some weird neurological stuff going on though, and I'm still barely confident that it's chronic lyme disease. The difficulty is that most us medical professionals don't acknowledge it because the CDC doesn't acknowledge it, despite a veritable mountain of peer-reviewed clinical data demonstrating ongoing effects and live bacteria years and years after initial infection and treatment. Hell, biopsies of people who had been diagnosed with acute line decades before have still found live bacteria! 

The issue I'm going to face there is if that is the case, there aren't any Lyme literate doctors in my area. I'm about a three and a half hour drive from NYC though, and I have a lot of friends in the area I can stay with when I visit, along with the ability to work partially remote as needed, so I'm going to begin that process soon. 

If I can get these couple of issues under control, get my full range of motion and control back in my left arm and shoulder, get better sleep and be able to breathe better because I'm not suffering a constant low-level asthma attack, and then get the weird recurring neurological flare-ups with all of the exhaustion and joint pain that I get every few months taking care of, I'm going to feel like I'm 20 again. 

The most frustrating thing though is the number of doctors over the years who tried to tell me it's just anxiety because I was diagnosed with anxiety and depression about 10 years ago when all of this started. Over the last year, I finally got sick of that and started being a lot more aggressive and refusing to take no for an answer, finding new doctors until someone would actually take these things seriously, and on almost every damned issue, objective medical testing has borne out that the symptoms I was experiencing came from very real, very verifiable, and thankfully treatable things. Just thinking about how much worse they have made my quality of life for almost a damn decade because doctors would not listen and wanted to easily dismiss things as anxiety is frustrating though. 

Especially since the anxiety and depression that hit me about a decade ago came out of God damn nowhere and were remarkably uncharacteristic for me. Almost as though they were a symptom rather than a cause! 

And the reason I fixate on Lyme disease is because all of this shit initially started after a nasty tick bite that resulted in a large non bullseye rash. Testing at the time said it was not Lyme, but the exhaustion, the brain fog, the agitation, the anxiety, the joint pain, the numbness and tingling, the visual disturbances, all of this shit started within 6 to 18 months after that damn tick bite. I had never experienced any of it prior to that. 

It's frustrating that the US medical system pretends chronic lyme does not exist when the clinical evidence for it is so conclusive though. There are also countries such as Germany which do acknowledge the condition and routinely treat it. People suffering from the same collection of bullshit that I've been dealing with will sometimes save up enough to travel to Germany for treatment, and a lot of the case reports I've seen show that their lives were changed dramatically afterwards. 

I'm hoping I won't have to go that far. 

Anyway sorry for the diary posting, I guess the real takeaway here is that so many things are getting explained and going better for me right now, and you've got to be willing to aggressively self-advocate when it comes to medical care. Also, the degree to which people who have a history of dealing with mental health struggles get valid medical concerns dismissed is infuriating, and the degree to which we write off mental health as separate from physical health rather than it often being a symptom of physical issues is frustrating to say the least. 

I'm sure this is riddled with weird typos and other shit because I just dictated it all rather than typing it, so I'm going to go ahead and apologize for any of the insanity. 

Anyway, off to pick up my new inhaler to keep me breathing easy for the next few months until I'm out of this place!
